Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient, an 83-year-old woman with a history of developmental disorders, presented to the emergency outpatient unit with a one-week history of dyspnea. She had heavily decreased breath sounds in the left lung. Chest radiograph and CT scan of the chest showed pleural effusions on the left lung. Two diagnostic thoracenteses were non-diagnostic, and a semirigid thoracoscopy was performed to visualize the pleura. Thoracoscopy revealed diffuse thickening of the parietal and visceral pleura, compatible with pleural dissemination with biopsy samples taken from only the visceral pleura node. Hematoxylin and eosin staining and immunohistochemical staining revealed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma with malignant neoplasm. 
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Disposition:
The patient was discharged to the care of her family. 

Condition:
The patient had a stable condition upon discharge. 

Clinical Course:
The patient required semirigid thoracoscopy with biopsy samples taken from only the visceral pleura node. Hematoxylin and eosin staining and immunohistochemical staining revealed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma.

Follow-up:
The patient was referred for follow-up care with an oncologist. 

Instructions:
The patient was instructed to follow-up with an oncologist. 

Treatment:
The patient underwent semirigid thoracoscopy for biopsy samples, which was successful. The treatment plan includes referral to an oncologist for further management. 

Complications:
No complications were noted during the hospitalization.

text:
**Principal diagnosis code: C34.9 – Malignant neoplasm of bronchus or lung, unspecified**

**Rationale:**
- The condition chiefly responsible for the work-up and the admission is lung adenocarcinoma, confirmed histologically (H&E and immunohistochemistry) on pleural biopsy.
- The pleural effusion and dyspnea are symptoms and manifestations of the malignancy. Under ICD-10-AM coding standards, they are not coded as the principal diagnosis once the underlying cause is established.
- The record gives no lobe or site within the lung, so the unspecified code C34.9 applies. If the lobe had been documented, a more specific code would be used (C34.1 for upper lobe, C34.3 for lower lobe, and so on).

**Suggested additional diagnoses:**
- **C78.7 – Secondary malignant neoplasm of pleura.** Thoracoscopy showed diffuse thickening of the parietal and visceral pleura "compatible with pleural dissemination." Code this only if the clinician documents it as metastatic pleural disease. The biopsy was taken from the visceral pleura only, so the documentation may be insufficient.
- **J91.0 – Malignant pleural effusion.** Code this if the effusion is documented as malignant. In ICD-10-AM it is coded in addition to the primary neoplasm.
- **F89 or the relevant F7x/F8x code.** The "developmental disorders" history can be coded if it is clinically relevant and documented.

**Procedure (ACHI):** Semirigid thoracoscopy with pleural biopsy. Check the ACHI index for the exact block, for example thoracoscopic pleural biopsy under the pleura procedures.

**Query for the clinician:** Confirm the lung site and whether pleural metastasis and malignant effusion are diagnosed. This would allow more specific coding.
